vote.question: Share of valid votes in Daliyat al-Karmel, Yarka, Beit Jann, Hurfeish, Kisra-Sumei, Yanuh-Jat, Peki'in, Julis, Sajur and Ein al-Asad combined, computed from the Central Elections Committee's locality files. These are village results, not the vote of a group.
vote.source: Central Elections Committee, results by locality (computed)
vote.note: Lists as they ran each year. Meretz ran within the Democratic Union in September 2019 (4.2%) and on a joint list with Labor–Gesher in March 2020. Non-Zionist lists are the Arab-led lists: Hadash–Ta'al and Ra'am–Balad (April 2019), the Joint List (2019–2021), Ra'am (2021–2022), Hadash–Ta'al and Balad (2022). The locality set follows the Moshe Dayan Center (https://dayan.org/he/content/5714); results files for earlier elections are at media21–media24.bechirot.gov.il. Counting Isfiya and leaving out Peki'in moves the 2022 shares by 1–2 points. IDI's own 2022 figures for Druze localities: National Unity 30.4, Yisrael Beiteinu 18.3, Meretz 14, Likud 10.6 (https://en.idi.org.il/articles/47986)

idi-2025.title: Druze, Muslim and Christian respondents compared, 2025

rows.label: The Supreme Court intervenes too much in government decisions

idi-2025.question: Share agreeing with each statement, by religion, within IDI's Arab sample.
idi-2025.source: Israel Democracy Institute, Israeli Democracy Index 2025
idi-2025.sample: 364 Arab respondents by phone in Arabic; Druze about 8.4%, roughly 31 people
idi-2025.note: IDI publishes these Druze, Muslim and Christian figures in its report (e.g. table 2.5) but says it "limited the use of" the religion breakdown "due to the small proportion of Christians and Druze in the Arab sample." The Druze subsample is about 31 people, so its margin of error is far wider than the full sample's
